stages.a: A colonized block, opened on its side.
stages.v: Golden oyster is side-fruited at Catawba Mushrooms.

stages.a: The pins branch like coral before any caps form.
stages.v: Golden primordia look coral-like on the blocks.

stages.a: Small caps open on slender stems, each one a shallow funnel.
stages.v: Goldens respond more to light than other oysters: they go toward the top of the rack.

stages.a: The caps open into thin funnels with wavy edges.
stages.v: Treat goldens like other oysters: pick before the caps flatten.

stages.a: The funnels open out flat and the edges thin and wave.
stages.v: Goldens look pretty but do not hold up in the pan. Shelf life is the drawback.

stages.a: The edges split and turn up.
stages.v: Golden oyster is invasive in places; low-spore strains are planned.

labels.a: The cut on the side of the bag.

labels.v: Golden primordia look coral-like on the blocks.

labels.a: Thin stems that branch from a shared base.
Each cap dips in the middle like a funnel.
The thin cap edge waves and ruffles.
Gills run down from the cap onto the stem.
The edge splits and curls up as the cap ages.
